intent: Supplement the metre-scaled GrassField PBR substrate with real silhouette-scale lamina geometry while keeping sub-pixel turf mass in the base material. Source QA is not rendered proof.

construction.landscapeType: maintained circa-2000 Japanese new-town common lawn
components: existing prepared turf/topsoil substrate represented by GrassField
grass crowns originating at the finish-grade datum
curved double-sided two-segment lamina blade geometry
combined 9 m patch meshes used only as a render batching boundary
construction.laminaThicknessRepresentation: Biological lamina thickness is below reliable benchmark pixel scale and is represented as explicitly double-sided surface geometry rather than a centimetre-scale solid slab.
construction.substrateInterface: Blade bases originate 4 mm above the zero-grade GrassField top to avoid coplanar z-fighting while remaining within the visible turf/contact zone; no blade receives a gameplay collider.
construction.mounting: Biological crowns are rooted into the existing lawn substrate. Patch roots are batching containers only and may not imply visible manufactured seams.
construction.interfacesGapsSeals: A 0.16 m construction-clearance margin excludes apartment, plaza, park-path and worn-path footprints so blades cannot visibly interpenetrate hardscape. There are no manufactured seals in the biological lawn assembly.
construction.orientationExposure: Upward/outward laminae receive coherent midsummer sun and sky fill; near-circulation edges are maintained shorter; shaded faces rely on scene fill, contact shadow and occlusion rather than painted darkness.
construction.aging: Ordinary mowing, dry-summer UV exposure, local shade and pedestrian-edge maintenance only. Variation is causal and does not introduce a narrative damage layer.
construction.geometryVsMaterial: Blade height, width, bend, lean, taper, double-sided silhouette and hardscape clearance are geometry. Chlorophyll/color breakup, fine venation-equivalent normal response and sub-pixel turf mass remain material/microtexture.
construction.manufactureReasoning: This is living planted turf rather than a manufactured panel: the reconstruction unit is crown-to-lamina growth from prepared grade, with explicit hardscape maintenance interfaces and blade-scale silhouette only where benchmark pixels can resolve it.

placement.densityRule: Each patch evaluates one fixed deterministic candidate budget. Rejected hardscape candidates are not retried, so exposed-lawn fraction controls geometric density instead of concentrating a full-patch population into narrow remnants.
placement.heightCausality: Accepted blades near hardscape/circulation edges receive a deterministic maintained-height reduction; open-lawn blades retain the wider nominal range.
placement.antiRepetition: Patch/candidate hashing changes position, height, width, yaw, bend and texture phase. Structural QA requires at least ten distinct LOD0 geometry signatures when ten or more patches are populated.

material.albedo: Inherit canonical grass albedo/microtexture without directional illumination marks or baked highlight streaks.
material.roughnessIntent: Dry cut grass remains predominantly rough; the inherited physical-data map is attenuated by smoothness scale 0.28 so isolated grazing response stays restrained.
material.microstructure: Inherited grass physical-data texture represents sub-pixel fibrous/chlorophyll breakup while explicit lamina geometry owns silhouette-scale bends and tips.
material.uvAging: Dry midsummer baseline with mild ordinary UV desaturation only; current wet sheen is zero.
material.angularFresnelResponse: At grazing angles, brightness may rise only from dielectric Fresnel plus the coherent SummerSun/sky/reflection state. Highlight direction may not be painted into albedo or masks.

lod.policy: Each lower LOD retains a deterministic prefix of the same accepted tuft set and strictly reduces tuft/vertex count. It may remove sub-pixel blades but may not reshuffle the retained lawn footprint between levels.

lighting.direct: Use the scene SummerSun only for directional key response and blade shadows.
lighting.fill: Use sky/ambient fill and probes for shadow-side readability.
lighting.contact: Blade bases must read as embedded in the turf substrate through contact shadow/occlusion, not as hovering cards.
lighting.reflection: Use synchronized scene reflection state; the lawn system does not author fake environment highlights.

failureInjection: replace an authored patch mesh with a primitive plane
enable emission on the blade material
add a collider under the grass detail root
duplicate one LOD0 geometry mesh across otherwise different patches
place blades inside a hardscape exclusion footprint

renderEvidenceRequired.additionalReview: Inspect 100% lawn-edge and grazing silhouettes plus temporal movement/LOD sequence before assigning any Visual Fidelity points.
rejectIf: lighting reads as painted rather than scene-driven

expectedVisualFidelityImpact.vegetationNaturalComplexity: medium-high expected improvement; not awarded until render review
expectedVisualFidelityImpact.textureMicrodetailTexelFidelity: small-medium expected improvement from geometry/material scale separation; not awarded
expectedVisualFidelityImpact.cinematicImageQuality: medium expected improvement in grazing silhouette and foreground depth; not awarded
expectedVisualFidelityImpact.temporalLodAliasingStability: implementation supports cross-fade but remains a render risk until temporal evidence is reviewed
